design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated using a random block design generated via the SAS 'ranuni' function with block size of 4.

domain_judgments.rationale: An appropriate computer-generated block randomization sequence was created and centrally assigned by an author not conducting clinical assessments, with balanced baseline characteristics between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The subjects in the present study were randomly and blindly assigned by author K.S. to either an exercise group (n = 40) or a wait-list (reference) group (n = 41) by means of a random block design. The SAS 'ranuni' function, generating random numbers with equal probability distribution, was programmed so that for each consecutive four participants, two were randomly allocated to the exercise group and two to the reference group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding of participants to exercise versus wait-list was not possible, adherence was high, no co-interventions were reported, and an intention-to-treat analysis was applied.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The exercise group received the same information except that the recommendation to 'wait and see' was replaced with a 3-month daily exercise regime performed at home... The subjects were asked to report if competing treatment was given, but none reported such treatment. Subjects were instructed not to use pain-relieving or anti-inflammatory medication other than paracetamol. Adherence to instructions and the intervention programme was monitored... The intention-to-treat approach was followed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Very few participants were lost to follow-up (2 in exercise, 1 in wait-list) and nearly complete data were available and analysed for all randomized participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the exercise group 93% participated in all follow-up visits and in the reference group 90%... Data loss owing to partial non-response (missing data in returned questionnaires and protocols) was 1%. The intention-to-treat approach was followed. The few missing data points were replaced with data from the nearest previous non-missing data measurement occasion.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcomes are subjective pain ratings (visual analogue scales) during provocation tests administered by an unblinded assessor who was also aware of participant group assignment, introducing a high risk of detection bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The same observer did all measurements. Since the observer also gave instructions about the exercise no blinded data collection was possible.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT00888225), registration occurred retrospectively in 2009 after study completion (2003-2006), and multiple pain and functional measures were analyzed without an accessible prespecified statistical analysis plan prior to trial commencement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial is registered at http://clinicaltrials.gov/ as NCT00888225.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high due to the lack of assessor and participant blinding for patient-reported subjective pain outcomes (VAS scores) assessed by the interventionist.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to three parallel groups using a computerized random number generator in permuted blocks of six with concealed telephone allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated using a computerized random number generator with permuted blocks and concealed off-site via telephone allocation, with well-balanced baseline characteristics.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We randomised participants by telephone via concealed allocation to physiotherapy, corticosteroid injections, or a wait and see group. The randomisation sequence (kept off site and drawn up by a computerised random number generator in permuted blocks of six) and group allocation were kept concealed from all study personnel throughout the entire study...

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants could not be blinded to physiotherapy vs injections vs wait-and-see, analyses were conducted on an intention-to-treat basis and deviations were minimal and did not affect trial conclusions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We did statistical analyses on a blinded, intention to treat basis with SPSS software (v11.0.0). We also did a per protocol analysis. ... Removal of participants who failed to adhere to the trial protocol only minimally changed the results of the intention to treat analysis

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up rates were exceptionally high across all groups (>92% in all arms at 52 weeks, 100% in injection arm), making bias due to missing data unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Wait and see: completed trial n=62 [of 67]; Corticosteroid injection: completed trial n=65 [of 65]; Physiotherapy: completed trial n=63 [of 66]

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors were blinded, primary outcomes included objective dynamometry and standardized scales, and assessor guessing was at chance levels (51%) with sensitivity analyses showing no bias from unblinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A blinded assessor who was not involved in the treatment allocation made the final selection and recorded baseline characteristics and measures. ... At 52 weeks, the blinded assessor correctly guessed the allocated treatment in 101/198 (51%) cases, on the basis of the course of elbow complaints and four participants who inadvertently revealed their group allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: All pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes were reported consistently across defined time points according to a documented statistical analysis strategy.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary outcome measures throughout the follow-up period were global improvement, pain-free grip force, and assessor's rating of severity. ... The primary end points for the trial were six weeks (short term) and 52 weeks (long term).

overall_summary: This trial was well-designed and executed, featuring robust computer-generated concealed randomisation, blinded outcome assessors, minimal loss to follow-up, and consistent intention-to-treat analysis across all pre-specified outcomes.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to three treatment groups using a computer program with a minimization strategy based on complaint duration.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was conducted via a computer program using a minimization strategy after enrollment by an independent researcher, ensuring sequence generation and allocation concealment, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After retrieval of informed consent, patients were included in the trial by the medical doctor (GK) and subsequently randomized by a researcher (PS) using a computer program with minimization strategy for the duration of complaints (ie, ≤3 months; 3-6 months, and ≥6 months).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants and physical therapists could not be blinded to the intervention, an intention-to-treat analysis was performed for all randomized patients and protocol deviations were minor and balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data were analyzed using both intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses. ... For the per-protocol analysis, a total of 17 patients who violated the treatment protocol were excluded. Similar results were found when compared to the intention-to-treat analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing outcome data were very minimal (4 of 180 patients at 6 weeks and less than 6% at 1 year) and balanced across groups, making bias highly unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At 6 weeks, 2 patients from group A and 1 patient from both group B and group C were lost to follow-up. ... The dropout rate was less than 6% after 1-year follow-up and thus kept to a minimum.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the physical exam assessor was successfully blinded, the primary outcomes (global improvement/success, pain, severity, disability) were subjective and self-reported by patients who were inherently aware of their assigned intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The blinded assessor (GK) assessed outcomes at 6 weeks and 1 year after randomization. In addition, a questionnaire was sent to patients at 26 weeks. ... Blinding of assessment was optimized by instructing the patients not to inform the blinded assessor when they received treatment. After each follow-up examination, the assessor was asked to guess the allocation and give the reasons for this.

domain_judgments.rationale: All predefined primary and secondary outcomes across all time points are fully reported in the results and tables according to the specified statistical plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data were analyzed using both an intention-to-treat and a per-protocol analysis. Changes in scores over time were calculated for each patient by subtracting the results at baseline from those at follow-up.

overall_summary: The trial was well conducted with computer-generated allocation concealment, low attrition, and an intention-to-treat analysis, but receives Some Concerns overall because participants could not be blinded to physical therapy versus bracing and the main outcomes were subjective participant-reported measures.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial in which participants were randomly allocated to either an exercise or control group using folded notes drawn from a container.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was performed by subjects picking folded notes from a container, which lacks secure concealment, although baseline characteristics were generally balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Allocation after the baseline examination was randomized by each subject picking from a container one of two folded notes showing either a 'one' (exercise group) or a 'two' (control group).

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were blinded to which intervention was under active investigation, adherence was high (>70%), and the dropouts occurred before the first follow-up due to unrelated reasons with no major deviations reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The blinded component concerned assigned treatment, i.e. subjects were not informed whether the allocated training or the forearm band was under investigation... The analysis was therefore conducted as per protocol.

domain_judgments.rationale: Dropout was relatively low (5/42, ~12%), balanced across groups (2 in exercise vs 3 in control), reasons were documented and baseline characteristics between dropouts and completers did not differ.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thirty-seven (88%) completed the mid-intervention follow-up at week 3 and 37 (88%) did so at the end of the intervention period at week 6. Four women and one male elected not to complete the trial before the first follow-up at week 3.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessment of pain-free strength relies on patient-reported onset of discomfort and manual dynamometer resistance, and it is unclear whether outcome assessors were blinded to group allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Both pain-free grip strength and isometric extensor strength were measured three times, each with a 30-s rest interval between each measurement. The mean value of the tests was used for further analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered in ClinicalTrials.gov and the reported primary and secondary outcomes correspond with the pre-specified protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was registered in the database ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT00975442).

overall_summary: Some concerns were identified regarding the randomization sequence concealment (picking folded notes from a container) and the measurement of subjective/effort-dependent outcomes without clear blinding of outcome assessors.

design_rationale: The authors explicitly state that participants were randomly allocated to one of four treatment groups using a predetermined sequence generated by a random numbers table with block randomization and opaque sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was randomly generated using a random numbers table, concealed using sequentially numbered opaque sealed envelopes, and baseline characteristics were reasonably balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The numbers were issued in a predetermined random sequence using a block size of 24 and generated by the use of a random numbers table, in such a way that each block consisted of the four treatment groups in equal proportions. The treatment group details were then sealed in a series of opaque numbered envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding was not feasible due to the nature of the interventions (injections vs physiotherapy vs observation), and the analysis excluded participants who did not complete the 7-week follow-up (complete-case analysis rather than intention-to-treat).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcome assessments were performed by the research physiotherapist before randomisation and 7 weeks after the actual start of the treatment. ... The differences in the mean changes between treatment groups at 7-week follow up for all the outcome measures was then analysed using a two-factor analysis of variance (with interaction).

domain_judgments.rationale: Substantial, differential loss to follow-up occurred (41% missing in the physiotherapy arms vs 0% in injection alone and 17% in observation), and missingness is likely related to the true outcome values without appropriate handling.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Another limitation of our study was the relatively high 10 of 24 (41%) drop out rate of patients from the two groups who had physiotherapy as part of their treatment regime [physiotherapy alone (n=5) and physiotherapy plus steroid injection (n=5)]. There is a strong likelihood that patients who failed to return for follow up would have better function and less pain, although we cannot be really sure as to the reasons.

domain_judgments.rationale: Assessors and participants were not blinded, and the primary and secondary outcomes (pain-free grip strength and PRFEQ) are subjective or effort-dependent participant-reported measures that could be influenced by knowledge of the assigned intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcome assessments were performed by the research physiotherapist before randomisation and 7 weeks after the actual start of the treatment. The primary outcome measure, pain free grip strength (PFGS), was measured in kilograms.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective trial registration or pre-specified statistical analysis plan is referenced, leaving open the potential for selective reporting of analyses or time points.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For all of the outcome measures studied, we subtracted baseline values from the values obtained at 7 weeks for each patient. The mean change from baseline for each of the treatment groups at 7-week follow up was calculated for each of the outcome measures studied.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high, primarily driven by substantial and differential missing outcome data across treatment arms (up to 41% attrition in groups receiving physiotherapy) which was not accounted for in the complete-case analysis, alongside unblinded assessment of subjective and effort-dependent outcomes.

design_rationale: Participants were allocated to groups using an alternating quasi-random method based on odd versus even medical registry numbers rather than a truly random allocation sequence.

domain_judgments.rationale: Key baseline characteristics were reported and showed no statistically significant differences between groups, though unmeasured or unadjusted residual confounding cannot be ruled out in this non-randomized quasi-allocation design.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: There was no significant difference between Group 1 and 2 in demographic information of race ((p=0.54)), gender ((p=0.22)), age ((p=0.59)), occupation ((p=0.45)), education level ((p=0.28)) or months in pain ((p=0.37)).

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were recruited consecutively among patients presenting for care, and selection into the study occurred before assignment without indication that selection was related to intervention and outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Between 2015 and 2017 all patients (refer to table 1 for demographic information) diagnosed with LET by orthopedic fellowship-trained hand surgeons and referred to therapy for non-operative management of the condition were offered the opportunity to participate in the study if they met eligibility requirements... Ninety-four patients were consented, enrolled and randomized to one of two groups according to their medical registry number

domain_judgments.rationale: The intervention groups were clearly defined and classified at baseline without risk of misclassification.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Ninety-four patients were consented, enrolled and randomized to one of two groups according to their medical registry number, with odd numbered registrants enrolled in Group 1 and even numbered registrants in Group 2. Medical registry numbers were assigned by front desk staff who were unaware of the study.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: Therapists and patients could not be blinded to the exercise interventions, and protocol deviations (such as extra visits or other treatments like injections) led to post-hoc exclusions rather than an intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients were treated by three therapists who were trained in and in agreement of all components of the rehabilitation program... In this study we maintained all patients at 4-6 visits for consistency between groups, but for the group who received no strengthening some of the visits were solely for the purpose of review and to check on the patient's status.

domain_judgments.rationale: There was substantial attrition (37% overall, with 47.5% in Group 2 vs 29.6% in Group 1) and patients were excluded post-allocation based on treatment adherence, interventions received (injections/surgery), or withdrawal, creating high potential for bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Group 1 had 54 patients and Group two had 40. Group 1 yielded 38 participants who were able to be followed for the full 52 weeks with complete or near complete data. Group 2 yielded 21. A total of 35 patients (37%) were either excluded or lost to follow up at 12 months.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were subjective patient-reported measures (NPRS and QuickDASH) assessed in unblinded participants who were fully aware of their assigned intervention group.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcome measures of 1) pain at rest and with activity and 2) QuickDASH scores were obtained at initial, 6 and 12 week visits. The same outcomes were collected by phone or email at 24 and 52 weeks after initiation of therapy.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective protocol registration or pre-published statistical analysis plan was cited, leaving potential for selective reporting of analyses across multiple time points.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Our primary outcome measure was pain at rest and pain with activity; our secondary measure was level of functional impairment as measured by the QuickDASH. Outcome measurements were assessed at baseline, 6, 12, 24 and 52 weeks post initiation of therapy.

overall_summary: The study has a serious overall risk of bias under ROBINS-I, driven primarily by serious bias due to missing data (37% attrition with substantial differential loss to follow-up and exclusions related to treatment adherence/subsequent interventions) alongside moderate risks from non-random allocation, unblinded participants reporting subjective outcomes, and lack of pre-registration.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to either the experimental group or the control group using an urn draw.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although an urn draw was used by an independent research assistant, there was a statistically significant baseline imbalance in the onset/duration of lateral epicondylitis between groups (22 vs 43 months).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A number assigned to each subject was placed in an opaque urn. A research assistant with no further implication in this study has drawn numbers to form the 2 groups... Both groups (experimental and control) are not equivalent because of the onset of the LE

domain_judgments.rationale: Due to the nature of the interventions (manual therapy vs advice/ergonomics), participants and the treating clinician could not be blinded, and deviations from intended interventions or non-protocol differences in care cannot be fully excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The clinician responsible of the study, a chiropractor completing a masters' degree in kinesiology, collected and managed all the data. He also provided all the treatment to the experimental group and the advice to the control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Differential dropout occurred exclusively in the control group (3 of 15, 20% vs 0% in the experimental group) and these participants were excluded from analysis rather than analyzed under intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Three subjects from the control group could not come back after the group assignment, so their data were not used because we only had their baseline data (Fig 2)... The possibility of an intention-to-treat analysis was evaluated, but because the missing data were too important, the subjects lost to follow-up were removed from the analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were assessed and managed by the unblinded clinician providing the interventions, and the primary and secondary outcomes (VAS, PRTEE, pain-free grip strength) involve subjective reporting and patient-clinician interaction that could be influenced by lack of blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The clinician responsible of the study, a chiropractor completing a masters' degree in kinesiology, collected and managed all the data. He also provided all the treatment to the experimental group and the advice to the control group... In this trial, all the statistical analyses were done by the clinician responsible to the study who has collected and managed all the data.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a pre-published trial protocol or prospectively registered analysis plan detailing the planned primary/secondary analyses before study completion.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome assessment was the PRTEE. The 2 secondary measurements were the PFG and the VAS.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high, primarily driven by substantial differential post-randomization attrition in the control group (20% dropouts excluded from analysis) and unblinded outcome assessment administered by the treating investigator for subjective and effort-dependent outcomes.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated using a computer-generated randomisation sequence with concealed opaque envelopes to either the exercise group or the wait-and-see group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed using opaque envelopes, administered by an independent researcher, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A computer-generated randomisation sequence was performed by a researcher not involved in data collection. Randomisation was stratified based on baseline worst pain ratings of 5 or less (low pain) or 6 or more (high pain) on an 11-point NRS. Following baseline measurements, participants were randomly allocated using concealed opaque envelopes to either the exercise or wait-and-see group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants could not be blinded to exercise vs wait-and-see, co-interventions were balanced and negligible, adherence was high, and an intention-to-treat approach was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All participants received a 20-minute individualised session with the trial physiotherapist who had a postgraduate Master's degree-level qualification. Participants were provided written and verbal general advice regarding self-management and ergonomics. Participants assigned to the exercise group received additional information and advice to complete an unsupervised program of isometric exercise in a home setting for 8 weeks. [...] Statistical analyses were performed on an intention-to-treat basis with Stata version 14 software

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 39 out of 40 participants (98% completion rate), so missing data is negligible and unlikely to bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Follow-up at 8 weeks was completed by 39 (98%) of 40 participants. One participant in the exercise group was not available to attend the 8-week follow-up session. For this participant, the primary outcomes PRTEE and pain-free grip strength could not be collected, however a GROC score was obtained via telephone.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the outcome assessor was blinded for physical measures, the primary outcomes PRTEE and GROC are patient-reported, and participants were aware of their intervention group assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcome measures were collected at baseline and at the 8-week follow-up time point by an assessor blinded to treatment allocation. Primary outcome measures were the Patient-Rated Tennis Elbow Evaluation [...] global rating of change [...] and pain-free grip strength (N) of the affected arm.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes were reported as planned, and analysis followed an appropriate protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was registered in the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trial Registry (ACTRN12615001136594). [...] Continuous outcome measures were analysed using linear regression, with group allocation as the fixed factor, and baseline value of the outcome and stratifying variable of baseline pain as covariates.

overall_summary: The study has some concerns overall due to potential bias in outcome measurement for participant-reported outcomes (PRTEE and GROC) in an open-label trial comparing exercise to wait-and-see. All other domains (randomization process, deviations from intended interventions, missing outcome data, and selection of reported results) were judged as low risk of bias.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to either the minimal occupational intervention or the usual general practice care control group using block randomization with a random sequence of numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated randomly in blocks of four and concealed using sealed envelopes opened only after written informed consent was obtained.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization to intervention or control was performed in advance by the project coordinator in blocks of four according to a predetermined random sequence of numbers, and was supplied to each general practice in sealed envelopes, which were opened by the GP after eligible cases had signed an informed consent form.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and care providers could not be blinded to the intervention, and 23 randomized participants were excluded before baseline/intervention without a true intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Twenty-three of the randomized cases did not return the baseline questionnaire, regretted participation or did not receive the intervention. A further 10 cases were lost during follow-up... Due to the design, no blinding to treatment could be done.

domain_judgments.rationale: Of the 289 randomized cases, 23 dropped out immediately and further attrition resulted in only 227 (78.5%) having 12-month data, with missing 12-month data handled by carrying forward 6-month scores.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In order to increase power, the scores of overall improvement for 12 cases registered at 6 months but missing at 1 yr were included in the analysis. The same was done for 10 cases with regard to a 50% reduction in pain score.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcomes were entirely subjective self-reports of improvement and pain by unblinded participants who were aware of their treatment assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome measures were self-reported overall development of the condition reported in follow-up questionnaires at 3, 6 and 12 months after inclusion in the trial... Due to the design, no blinding to treatment could be done. The primary outcome assessment was done independently, based on patient self-reports in follow-up questionnaires.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or pre-specified statistical analysis plan is referenced, raising some concerns regarding potential selection of reported analyses or cutoffs (e.g., dichotomizations at upper quartiles).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A randomized controlled trial was performed in a cohort of 266 consecutive new cases of lateral epicondylitis diagnosed in general practice. Workplace factors were assessed with questionnaires at the time of inclusion, and patients completed follow-ups at 3, 6 and 12 months.

overall_summary: The trial has some concerns overall due to lack of blinding for subjective self-reported outcomes, post-randomization exclusions without an intention-to-treat approach, and lack of a pre-published trial analysis protocol.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three treatment groups using a computerized random number generator with block randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization sequence was computer-generated, allocation was concealed using opaque sealed envelopes handled by an independent assistant, and baseline characteristics were balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We used a computerised random number generator to draw up an allocation schedule. Block randomisation (permuted blocks of three) was done after prestratification for the duration of complaints (<=13 weeks or >13 weeks) and research centre. The assignment of patients to corticosteroid injections, physiotherapy, or a wait-and-see policy took place after final selection by the research physiotherapist and baseline assessment. An administrative assistant allocated interventions via opaque sealed envelopes marked according to the allocation schedule.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding of participants and treaters was not possible given the intervention types, care was delivered pragmatically according to protocol with minor deviations, and analysis was conducted on an intention-to-treat basis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The principal analysis was done on an intention-to-treat basis. Furthermore, we did an alternative analysis, excluding all patients who had not been treated according to protocol.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up was remarkably complete, with only 2 of 185 randomized patients (1.1%) lost to follow-up over 52 weeks.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the two patients who withdrew from the study, one had fully recovered and the other was not satisfied with treatment. ... Figure 1: 59 completed trial (wait-and-see), 60 completed trial (corticosteroid injection, 2 withdrew), 64 completed trial (physiotherapy).

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcomes were largely patient-reported (general improvement, pain, disability) where patients were unblinded to their treatment, and research physiotherapists were partially unblinded in some assessments.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The research physiotherapist was unaware of the allocated intervention. Before every assessment, patients were asked by the administrative assistant not to reveal any information about their treatment. Immediately after every assessment, the research physiotherapist was asked to guess the allocated treatment, and state any reasons for their assumption.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes and time points were clearly pre-specified and reported comprehensively according to the trial protocol without evidence of selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We assessed all outcomes at 3, 6, 12, 26, and 52 weeks. The principal analysis was done on an intention-to-treat basis. ... We used MANOVA for repeated measures to prevent multiple testing and to ascertain differences between the intervention with respect to the course of elbow complaints.

overall_summary: The study was a well-conducted randomized controlled trial with robust sequence generation, allocation concealment, low attrition, and an intention-to-treat analysis. However, there are some concerns regarding outcome measurement due to the subjective, patient-reported nature of the primary outcomes in participants who were unblinded to their assigned intervention.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three treatment groups using a computerized numeric block randomization schedule with variable block sizes prepared by an independent researcher and concealed allocation via an independent research assistant.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated via computerized block randomization with variable block size and allocation concealment was ensured by an independent research assistant, with baseline characteristics well-balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A computerised randomisation schedule was prepared by an independent researcher (ML), using numeric block randomisation with variable block size... Only then was an independent research assistant contacted, who, by consulting the previously prepared randomisation schedule, allocated the patient to one of three treatments ensuring concealed allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: While injections were double-blinded, patients could not be blinded to physiotherapy versus wait-and-see control, and non-protocol interventions (such as additional physiotherapy) differed significantly between groups during follow-up, which could introduce bias in this open-label physical intervention trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients were not blinded to the physiotherapy treatment, and that may have influenced outcome... The statistical analysis was performed blinded to treatment group on an intention-to-treat basis...

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up was high (89% completed at 52 weeks), missing data rates were low and balanced across groups (7 vs 5 vs 8 participants), and sensitivity analyses/GEE modeling under MCAR were applied.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 177 patients were included in the study. The trial was completed in June 2013, with 157 patients (89 %) completing the primary outcome at 52 weeks follow-up... Lost to follow up: Corticosteroid n=7, Placebo n=5, Control n=8.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (self-reported treatment success on a Likert scale) is subjective and evaluated by patients who were aware of whether they received active physiotherapy versus wait-and-see control.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome measures were the patients' evaluations of improvement after six, 12, 26, and 52 weeks... The patients were not blinded to the physiotherapy treatment, and that may have influenced outcome.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, followed an established published protocol, and reported the prespecified primary and secondary outcomes and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A randomized, placebo-controlled trial was conducted in a primary care setting in the city of Sarpsborg, Norway, as outlined in the published protocol [19]... Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT00826462

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is rated as some concerns, driven primarily by the lack of blinding of participants to the physiotherapy intervention relative to the wait-and-see control, which may affect the subjective self-reported primary outcome and co-interventions.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three treatment arms using Randomizer software with allocation concealment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization was performed using dedicated software with allocation concealment, and baseline characteristics did not show significant differences between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomized with allocation concealment using Randomizer→ software by MEDSHARING, 44 Rue Roger Salengro, 94120 Fontenay Sous Bois, France, http://www.ercf-medsharing.com/(cited 27.10.2020).

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and intervention providers could not be blinded given the nature of physical interventions (manual therapy, brace, TENS), and adherence or unmonitored co-interventions such as analgesic use were acknowledged as not evaluated.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Although pain medications (including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDs]) are recommended in the German guidelines, they were not included in this study... Finally, this study did not evaluate the use of concomitant medications, such as analgesics.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 52 randomized participants appear to have outcome data reported at baseline, 4 weeks, and 8 weeks post-treatment across all groups with no reported dropouts.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 52 patients included in this study, 18 received MT, 15 received a combination of TENS and FB, and 19 received a combination of MT, TENS, and FB (Table 3)... The number of participants required for the total sample was 52.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the physician evaluating outcomes was blinded, primary and secondary outcomes (VAS, PRTEE, SF-36) are patient-reported and participants were not blinded to their assigned intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The physician (corresponding author) evaluating the patient outcomes was blinded to the patient groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered retrospectively in 2020 (ethics approval was in 2012), meaning there was no pre-specified prospective analysis plan available prior to trial commencement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: retrospectively registered as a clinical trial (German Clinical Trial Register: DRKS, trial registration number: 00021137, date of registration 24/03/2020).

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to unblinded participants reporting subjective outcomes (VAS, PRTEE, SF-36), potential unmonitored co-interventions (analgesics), and retrospective trial registration without an accessible prospective analysis plan.
